result.title: Binding Paraphrased Instructions to Encountered Objects in sLLM Agents under Partial Observability
result.summary: Reliable deployment of LLM agents requires grounding diverse user expressions in their environments. Although RL-finetuned smaller large language model (sLLM) agents rival larger prompted LLMs on embodied tasks, their robustness to instruction paraphrases remains unclear. We introduce ALFWorld-Para to evaluate this robustness under controlled paraphrases, revealing 21-52% declines in success rates (SRs), predominantly driven by object synonyms. Despite retaining knowledge of synonym referents, agents often fail to take the corresponding objects even after observing them, exposing a gap between referential knowledge and object binding. Partial observability further complicates binding, as referents may remain unseen or have already been encountered under different labels. To address this challenge, we propose BINDIntent, a training-free framework that probabilistically binds referring expressions to observed labels using semantic proximity and estimated persistence against unseen candidates. Without additional training or LLM calls, BINDIntent improves synonym-paraphrase success of RL-finetuned sLLMs by 17.5-49.1 percentage points (pp) with only 0.4 ms of CPU overhead per step. It also raises GiGPO-7B's overall SR from 61.8% to 77.4%, surpassing a prompted 24B LLM. Code and benchmark are available at https://github.com/cau-hai-lab/ALFWorld-Para.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 ALFWorld-Para 基准，考察 RL 微调的小模型具身智能体对指令改写的鲁棒性，发现性能下降主要源于物体同义词；并提出免训练的 BINDIntent，用语义接近度与对未见候选的持续性估计概率化地把指代表达绑定到已观察标签上。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯文本具身任务，但「保有同义词指称知识却未在行动中使用」的绑定缺口与 LVR 中表示含信息却未被生成利用的问题相似；其持久性估计与部分可观测下的状态维护机制可供核查是否能迁移到视觉证据筛选与信念更新。
